newsitem.title: USA: LG&E unit wins 4-yr Texas power supply deal.
newsitem.headline: LG&E unit wins 4-yr Texas power supply deal.

text.p: LG&E Power Marketing Inc has signed a four-year contract to provide peaking capacity and electricity to two Texas power cooperatives, starting June 1, 1997, the company said Tuesday in a statement.

The agreement with South Texas Electric Cooperative Inc (STEC) and Medina Electric Cooperative will deliver up to 25 megawatts (MW) in 1997 and up to 50 MW by 2000 to the 300-MW STEC-Medina power pool.
Further terms of the contract, signed after a competitive bidding round, were not disclosed.
STEC serves the Jackson, Karnes, Nueces, San Patricio, Victoria and Wharton County electric ditribution cooperatives in southern Texas.
Its power pool partner, Medina Electric Cooperative, in Hondo, Texas, serves 17 southern Texas counties.
LG&E Power Marketing, based in Fairfax, Va., is an indirect, wholly owned subsidiary of LG&E Energy Corp in Louisville, Ky.
